headline: Sensex gains over 510 points, Nifty nears 25,300 supported by foreign inflows and lower crude oil

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign fund inflows and FII buying supported the market rally.
Lower crude oil prices helped boost investor sentiment.
The Indian rupee strengthened against the U.S. dollar.
Positive economic signals, including India's unemployment rate easing to 4.9% in October.
whatHappening: Sensex surged over 510 points while Nifty50 closed at 25,291.
Rupee appreciated 27 paise to close at 93.92 against the U.S. dollar.
FinMin and CBDT are examining suggestions for changes in equity capital gains tax.
SEBI is considering raising the foreign portfolio investor (FPI) beneficial ownership threshold to 25%.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices closed significantly higher on November 16, driven by foreign institutional buying and falling crude oil prices.
Sensex rallied over 510 points while Nifty topped the 25,290 level led by FMCG and key large-cap stocks.
Meanwhile, the rupee appreciated 27 paise against the US dollar amid reduced volatility and sustained foreign inflows.
